title: Generate a ready-to-use Kleinanzeigen title and description for sell/give-away items
description:
Right now the app gets a user to "decided" (sell/give-away/throw-away + suggested price) and stops -- the user still has to write their own Kleinanzeigen listing text from scratch. This epic adds an LLM-generated, ready-to-paste title and description for items the user will actually list on Kleinanzeigen, so the app's output is directly actionable, not just a recommendation.

Design decisions fixed for this epic (do not re-litigate in individual beads):

- **Scope: generated for decision=SELL and decision=GIVE_AWAY only.** Both are cases where the user will manually create a Kleinanzeigen listing (per this app's existing "the app never posts to Kleinanzeigen for you, you always list manually" design -- give-away items go under Kleinanzeigen's "zu verschenken" category, same manual-listing workflow as a sale). decision=THROW_AWAY never gets generated text (there's no listing to make) -- suggested_title/suggested_description simply stay null for those items, same as they do for anything not yet decided.
- **New nullable Item columns**: `suggested_title: str | None` and `suggested_description: str | None`, plain `Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String, nullable=True)` columns matching this codebase's existing style for `identified_name`/`category`/etc. -- not a JSON blob, not folded into an existing column. Requires a new Alembic migration (the tooling now exists, sandbox-64f) -- this one is straightforward: a normal `alembic revision --autogenerate` against current models plus the two new columns, no legacy-shape-detection complexity needed this time, since Alembic is already tracking `head` end to end (including on the live Railway deployment, which self-heals via `python -m app.db_migrate` on next deploy).
- **Language: German.** Kleinanzeigen's actual audience is German-speaking; a "ready to use" listing must be in German even though this app's other LLM prompts (identification) are in English. Fix this explicitly in the generation prompt.
- **Title length: target <=65 characters** (Kleinanzeigen's real listing-title UI limit), enforced with a code-level safety clamp after generation -- not just a prompt instruction the model might ignore. Description has no hard platform limit; keep it reasonably concise (a few sentences: what it is, condition, why selling/giving away, price framing) rather than open-ended.
- **New service, text-only Claude call, no photo re-sent.** New module (e.g. `app/listing_text.py`), mirroring `app/identification.py`'s existing Provider-protocol + injectable-fake pattern for testability (`IdentificationProvider`/`ClaudeVisionProvider`/`ItemIdentificationService` is the template to follow: a Protocol for the raw LLM call, a real provider with a lazily-constructed Anthropic client so import never requires `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, and a Service class that orchestrates + never raises). Input to the LLM call: `identified_name`, `category`, `brand`, `condition`, `search_keywords`, `decision`, `suggested_price`, and (optionally, if it improves output quality without much added complexity) a couple of comparable-listing titles for tone/style reference. No new image/vision API call -- this is a text-generation task over already-known structured data, not a re-identification task. Reuses the same `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`/model config already used by identification (no new env var for model selection).
- **Fully graceful degradation, never blocks the pipeline.** No `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, an LLM error, or any other failure in this stage must leave `suggested_title`/`suggested_description` as `None` and NOT raise, NOT change `Item.status`, and NOT prevent the item from reaching `decided` -- this stage is a best-effort enhancement layered on top of an already-complete pipeline outcome, exactly like every other graceful-degradation case already documented in this app ("How the pipeline behaves without a working step").
- **Ordering invariant: by the time a client observes `status=decided` via a GET, `suggested_title`/`suggested_description` (if generation succeeds) are already present in that same response -- no follow-up poll needed.** Confirmed achievable with a small, low-risk change: `app/pricing.py`'s `PricingDecisionService.decide_item(item)` already sets `item.status = ItemStatus.DECIDED` itself (in memory) before `app/pipeline.py`'s stage 3 calls `session.commit()` -- so the new listing-text stage just needs to run in `pipeline.py` AFTER `decide_item(item)` returns and BEFORE that existing `session.commit()` call. No restructuring of `pricing.py` itself is needed.
- **No new ItemStatus value, no change to the state machine or polling contract.** `suggested_title`/`suggested_description` being null is not a distinguishable pipeline state a client polls for -- it's just "not generated" (skipped because throw_away, or generation failed). Do not add a new status, do not change `MANUAL_STATUS_TRANSITIONS`, do not change the documented GET /items/{id} polling contract.
- **Frontend: display when present, with a copy-to-clipboard convenience affordance**, since "ready to use... post directly" implies minimizing friction to actually use it. Nothing rendered when null (matches this app's existing optional-field convention, e.g. how `item.hint` is rendered).

title: Gate /items* and /uploads/* behind require_user; fix all resulting test fallout
description:
Depends on sandbox-dfr.2 (the require_user dependency must already exist and work, proven by /auth/me's own tests). Files: backend/app/main.py, every existing backend test file that calls a route this bead gates.

This is the largest bead in the epic: gating routes is a two-line diff per route, but every existing test that hits a now-protected route will start failing with 401s the moment the dependency is attached, and fixing that fallout is this bead's real work. Do this as ONE bounded, atomic change -- do not leave an intermediate commit where routes are gated but tests are red.

1. Attach `Depends(require_user)` to every one of these routes in backend/app/main.py:
   - `POST /items` (create_item)
   - `GET /items` (list_items)
   - `GET /items/{id}` (get_item)
   - `PATCH /items/{id}/status` (update_item_status, or whatever it's actually named -- grep to confirm)
   Do NOT gate `GET /health`. Do NOT gate the three new `/auth/*` routes (already correctly scoped in sandbox-dfr.2).

2. Gate `GET /uploads/{filename}` (the `_UploadsStaticFiles` mount at `UPLOAD_URL_PREFIX`). This one is NOT a normal `@app.get(...)` route -- it's an ASGI sub-application mounted via `app.mount(...)`, so a plain `Depends(...)` doesn't apply to it directly. Add a small ASGI middleware (e.g. a `BaseHTTPMiddleware` subclass, or a plain `@app.middleware("http")` function -- pick whichever fits this codebase's existing style, there is no middleware yet besides `CORSMiddleware`, so establish a clean, well-commented pattern) that: for any request whose path starts with `UPLOAD_URL_PREFIX` (already a module constant -- reuse it, don't hardcode "/uploads"), checks the `Authorization` header the SAME way `require_user` does (reuse `verify_session_token` from app.auth directly -- do not duplicate the Bearer-parsing logic separately; consider factoring a tiny shared helper if that avoids duplication cleanly, but don't over-abstract for two call sites). If missing/invalid, return a 401 JSON response directly from the middleware (matching this codebase's error-response shape, e.g. `{"detail": "..."}"`) WITHOUT calling `call_next` (so the StaticFiles app underneath never even runs for an unauthorized request -- this also means an unauthorized request never gets the chance to leak information via response timing/error differences from the static file lookup itself). For any other path, call `call_next` unchanged. Add this middleware BEFORE (registered earlier than, or however this framework orders it -- verify empirically) the existing `app.mount(...)` call takes effect, and confirm via a test that an authorized request to an existing uploaded file still succeeds end-to-end through both the middleware and the static serving logic.

3. Now fix every existing test that breaks. Systematically find them: run the full suite first (`cd backend && source .venv/bin/activate && python -m pytest -q`) and use the failures list as your starting point, then grep test files for `client.get("/items`, `client.post("/items`, `client.patch("/items`, `client.get(f"/items`, `client.get("/uploads`, `client.get(f"{UPLOAD_URL_PREFIX}` etc. across ALL test files (test_items_upload.py, test_items_list_and_status.py, test_uploads_static.py, test_cors.py, and any others using TestClient against these routes) to make sure you catch every call site, not just the ones that show up as failures with a misleading error (some may fail with an assertion on response shape rather than an obvious 401, if the test doesn't explicitly check status code first).

4. Add a shared, reusable test fixture for minting a valid Bearer header in tests -- put it wherever this codebase's existing shared fixtures live (check for a conftest.py; if none exists, consider whether one should be introduced now given this is needed across many test files, or keep it as a small importable helper function in a shared test-utils module -- use your judgment based on what's cleanest given the existing test file structure, and explain your choice briefly). This fixture should produce `{"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}` where `token` is a real, valid session token for some whitelisted-for-this-fixture test email (e.g. mint it directly via `app.auth.issue_session_token("test@example.com")`, and monkeypatch `ALLOWED_EMAILS`/whatever the current test needs so that email is considered whitelisted where relevant -- though for routes gated by `require_user`, whitelisting doesn't matter at the point of using an already-issued session token, since `verify_session_token` only checks the token's own signature/expiry, not ALLOWED_EMAILS again -- confirm this understanding is correct by re-reading sandbox-dfr.1's `verify_session_token` implementation before assuming it).

5. Update every existing test call to a now-gated route to pass `headers=auth_headers` (or whatever the fixture/helper is named) alongside its existing request. Also ADD new negative tests (at least one per gated route family is enough, don't exhaustively duplicate across every single existing test) proving: calling `POST /items`, `GET /items`, `GET /items/{id}`, `PATCH /items/{id}/status`, and `GET /uploads/{filename}` WITHOUT an Authorization header returns 401, and that the underlying action did NOT happen (e.g. an unauthenticated POST /items must not create an Item row or write a photo file -- verify this, don't just check the status code).

6. Run the full backend pytest suite (`cd backend && source .venv/bin/activate && python -m pytest -q`) repeatedly until everything passes -- report the final exact count and confirm zero failures, zero skips introduced to dodge a real problem.

Done-criteria: all four /items* routes and GET /uploads/{filename} require a valid session (401 without one, and no side effects occur on a rejected request), GET /health and the three /auth/* routes remain unauthenticated, every previously-passing test still passes (now with an added auth header where needed), new negative tests prove each gated route family actually rejects unauthenticated requests, full pytest suite green with the exact final count reported.
close_reason: Gated POST/GET/PATCH /items* via Depends(require_user); gated GET /uploads/* via a new middleware that reuses require_user directly and returns 401 before the StaticFiles mount ever runs. Reviewer independently proved the middleware genuinely intercepts (instrumented the mount, confirmed 0 invocations on a rejected request, real file bytes on an authorized one) and, critically, mutation-tested the path-traversal tests by defeating the traversal guard directly -- 4 of them failed with '200 (traversal succeeded)' rather than 401, proving they still test containment and weren't silently neutered into auth-only checks. 209/209 passing. Flagged (not fixed here, follow-up filed) that plain tags can't send a Bearer header, so photo rendering needs a different auth mechanism for that one route.

title: Gate app access behind Google Sign-In with an email whitelist
description:
Currently POST/GET/PATCH /items* and GET /uploads/* are open to anyone who can reach the deployed backend URL. This epic adds Google Sign-In gating: only whitelisted emails (e.g. alexey.sinyakov@gmail.com) can obtain a session and use the app.

Design decisions fixed for this epic (do not re-litigate in individual beads):

- **Flow**: Google Identity Services (GIS) client-side JS widget obtains a Google-signed ID token (JWT) -- no OAuth redirect flow, no client secret needed on our side. Frontend POSTs that ID token to our backend, which verifies it against Google's public keys (google-auth library), checks email_verified is true and the email is in the ALLOWED_EMAILS whitelist, then issues our OWN signed session token.
- **Session transport: Bearer token in a custom Authorization header, stored in localStorage -- NOT a cookie.** The frontend (frontend-production-650a.up.railway.app) and backend (backend-production-c189.up.railway.app) are different up.railway.app subdomains, which browsers treat as cross-site for cookie purposes (SameSite=None would be required, and is increasingly unreliable under browsers' third-party-cookie restrictions). A bearer token sidesteps this entirely, works identically regardless of cross-site status, and needs zero change to the existing CORS config (allow_headers=["*"] in app/main.py already permits an Authorization header cross-origin).
- **Fail-closed, not fail-open.** If ALLOWED_EMAILS is unset or empty, ALL sign-in attempts must be rejected (403), regardless of what email is in a valid Google token -- this is the opposite default from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY's graceful degradation, because this is a security gate, not an optional feature. An admin must explicitly opt in a set of emails.
- **Env vars** (new): GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID (backend runtime -- verifies the ID token's "aud" claim) and VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID (frontend build-time, Vite-baked, same underlying value -- passed to the GIS widget so it knows which OAuth client to use), ALLOWED_EMAILS (backend runtime, comma-separated, case-insensitive match, same parsing convention as the existing ALLOWED_ORIGINS/_parse_allowed_origins), SESSION_SECRET (backend runtime, used to sign our own session tokens -- must be a real secret in production, not committed anywhere).
- **What's gated**: every /items* route (POST /items, GET /items, GET /items/{id}, PATCH /items/{id}/status) and GET /uploads/{filename} (photo serving). NOT gated: GET /health (Railway's health check needs it reachable with no auth).
- **Google OAuth Client ID creation is a manual, external, one-time step the user does in Google Cloud Console** -- not a bead in this epic. No bead should be blocked waiting for the real value; code and tests must work with any GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID value (verified via a mocked/fake token-verification call in tests, matching this codebase's existing pattern for ClaudeVisionProvider's fake Anthropic client).
- **Session token format**: implementer's choice of a signed, tamper-evident token (e.g. itsdangerous's URLSafeTimedSerializer, or a JWT via PyJWT) encoding the user's email + issued-at, with a fixed expiry (e.g. 7 days) -- no refresh-token complexity, a user just signs in again after expiry. Pick a small, well-known library rather than hand-rolling token signing.
- **Known, explicitly out-of-scope follow-up**: actually setting the new env vars on the live Railway deployment is a separate ops action once Railway MCP access is available again -- do not attempt it from any bead in this epic.

title: Fix upgrade_to_head() misdetecting a legacy DB that already matches head schema
description: backend/app/db_migrate.py's upgrade_to_head() currently assumes: no alembic_version table + items table already exists => the DB is at the pre-hint BASELINE shape, so it stamps at revision 304649b20ea1 unconditionally, then upgrades. This is wrong whenever the existing DB's items table was actually created via Base.metadata.create_all() using CURRENT (post-hint) models.py -- i.e. it already has the user_hint column, but was created/last touched before Alembic tracking existed. In that shape, stamping at baseline and then running the add_user_hint migration re-runs 'ALTER TABLE items ADD COLUMN user_hint' against a column that already exists, raising 'OperationalError: duplicate column name: user_hint' and exiting non-zero. Found live by the reviewer during sandbox-64f.4's review, reproduced against the local dev DB. Combined with sandbox-64f.4's fail-closed Docker CMD (python -m app.db_migrate && uvicorn ...), a DB in this shape would prevent the container from ever starting.
acceptance_criteria: upgrade_to_head() distinguishes the two possible untracked-but-existing-items-table shapes instead of assuming baseline unconditionally: inspect whether the existing items table already has the user_hint column (e.g. via SQLAlchemy inspector's get_columns), and stamp at HEAD (not baseline) when it already matches the current full schema, or at baseline when it doesn't (existing behavior, unchanged for that case). A new test covers this exact shape: build a DB via Base.metadata.create_all() against CURRENT models.py directly (no Alembic involved, matching how a real create_all()-based legacy DB would look), confirm it has user_hint and no alembic_version table, call upgrade_to_head(), and assert it succeeds (no OperationalError) and lands at head with the pre-existing data intact. The three previously-passing states (fresh, pre-hint-legacy-with-data-preservation, idempotent-rerun) must still pass unmodified. This logic must generalize correctly if more migrations are added later (i.e. don't hardcode to 'exactly these two shapes' if a cheap general solution exists -- but don't over-engineer a full schema-diffing framework either; matching against the migration chain's own head metadata via inspector comparison, or checking down the revision chain for the first stamp point whose schema the existing DB already satisfies, are both reasonable -- implementer's judgment, document the choice).
close_reason: Fixed upgrade_to_head() to inspect the existing items table for the user_hint column before deciding whether to stamp at baseline or head, instead of assuming baseline unconditionally. Reviewer independently reproduced the original bug (duplicate column name error against a create_all()-built legacy DB) and confirmed the fix resolves it, all 5 db_migrate tests pass, 177/177 full suite. Updated the module docstring's stale two-shape description directly (trivial nit).

title: Introduce Alembic migrations for evolving the backend schema
description:
backend/app/db.py currently documents a deliberate choice to skip Alembic: 'we use Base.metadata.create_all() instead of Alembic ... If/when we need to evolve the schema of a populated DB without losing data ... that's the point to introduce Alembic -- track that as a follow-up bead rather than adding the machinery preemptively.' That moment has arrived: sandbox-iec.1 added Item.user_hint, and create_all() cannot add a column to an already-existing table -- any already-deployed DB (e.g. the live Railway backend's persistent-volume SQLite file) now silently lacks that column and will error on first query touching it. This epic adds Alembic so future schema changes can evolve a populated DB safely, and, as a direct side effect, gives us a real mechanism to reconcile that already-broken Railway DB.

Design decisions fixed for this epic (do not re-litigate in individual beads):

1. **Division of responsibility, unchanged startup path.** app/main.py's lifespan() keeps calling init_db(engine) (Base.metadata.create_all()) EXACTLY as it does today -- zero changes to lifespan(), zero changes to any test (many tests instantiate TestClient(app), which triggers this path; changing it risks the whole suite). create_all() keeps doing what it's structurally good at: creating missing tables on a fresh DB, safely and idempotently. Alembic's job is the thing create_all() cannot do: adding/altering columns on a table that already exists in a populated DB. Both mechanisms coexist; running create_all() after Alembic has already brought a DB to the current schema is a safe no-op (it only creates missing tables, never touches existing ones).

2. **Tests are unaffected.** No test may be changed to route through Alembic. Tests keep constructing engines and calling Base.metadata.create_all() directly, exactly as they do today (see backend/tests/test_models.py, test_cors.py, test_items_upload.py). Alembic is exercised by its own dedicated tests only (see task 3).

3. **DB URL: single source of truth.** Alembic's env.py must NOT hardcode or re-derive the DB path independently -- extract the URL-computation logic already in app/db.py's make_engine()/_default_db_path() (which already respects the DATA_DIR env var) into a small reusable function, e.g. get_database_url() -> str, and have both make_engine() and Alembic's env.py call it. One source of truth, so Alembic always points at the exact same DB the running app would use.

4. **Two-revision migration chain, autogenerated, not hand-written.** Revision 0001 (baseline) must reconstruct the FULL schema as it existed BEFORE sandbox-iec.1 (i.e. every table as originally defined, items WITHOUT user_hint) -- this exactly matches any already-deployed pre-this-epic DB, so it can be safely "stamped" onto one as a true no-op. Revision 0002 adds the user_hint column, matching sandbox-iec.1 exactly. Both must be generated via alembic revision --autogenerate (never hand-typed column definitions -- autogenerate reads the real SQLAlchemy model metadata, so it can't drift from the actual types/nullability/etc.). See task 2 for the exact recipe to produce them correctly. Going forward, all NEW migrations (schema changes after this epic) are generated the normal way: change the model, alembic revision --autogenerate, review, commit -- no more two-step baseline tricks needed once the chain exists.

5. **Reconciling an already-existing, pre-Alembic DB is a first-class, tested code path, not a manual one-off.** A DB that already has the items table but no alembic_version tracking table (i.e. any DB created before this epic) must be automatically detected and stamped at 0001 (a true no-op against that exact schema) before upgrade head runs -- see task 3 for the exact logic. A completely fresh/empty DB just runs upgrade head from scratch (0001 then 0002). A DB already tracked and at head is a no-op. All three cases must be covered by tests using real temp SQLite files, not mocks.

6. **Wired into deploy, not app-import-time.** The upgrade step (task 3's entrypoint) runs as an explicit pre-start step in the Docker CMD (shell-form, chained with && -- this repo's Dockerfile.railway files already use shell-form CMD specifically so ${PORT} expands, so &&-chaining works the same way), NOT inside lifespan()/app import time. This keeps it out of the test-suite's code path entirely (see decision 1) while still running automatically on every Railway/Docker deploy and being available as an explicit manual command for native/local runs.

Known follow-up, explicitly out of scope for this epic: this epic gives us the TOOL to fix the live Railway DB (stamp 0001 + upgrade head), but actually running it against the live deployment is a separate ops action -- the Railway MCP connection is currently unavailable in this session. Do not attempt to reach the live Railway deployment from any bead in this epic; that happens once tooling lands and Railway access is available again.

title: Add optional text hint alongside photo upload to guide item identification
description:
Right now POST /items only accepts a photo; the vision-identification prompt (app/identification.py) has zero user-supplied context. Users often know something the vision model can't see from the photo alone (brand, what it is, a model number written on the underside, etc.) -- this epic adds an OPTIONAL free-text hint the user can type alongside the photo, which flows through: UploadPage (frontend) -> POST /items multipart field -> Item.user_hint DB column -> ItemIdentificationService/ClaudeVisionProvider (prompt augmentation) -> back out via GET /items/{id} serialization -> shown on the result page.

Design decisions fixed for this epic (do not re-litigate in individual beads):
- Multipart form field name: 'hint'. DB column name: 'user_hint' (avoids shadowing the word 'hint' as a bare Python identifier elsewhere, and matches this codebase's existing pattern of prefixing ambiguous names, e.g. 'identified_name'). Serialized JSON key: 'hint' (matches the form field name, not the DB column name -- consistent with how identified_name/photo_path etc. are already exposed under their own JSON keys, not raw column names).
- Optional, always: omitting it, or submitting an empty/whitespace-only string, must behave IDENTICALLY to today (item.user_hint stays None, prompt is unchanged byte-for-byte) -- no existing behavior may regress.
- Server-side validation: trim leading/trailing whitespace; treat empty-after-trim as None; reject (400) anything longer than 500 characters after trimming. 500 is an arbitrary but fixed cap -- use it, don't invent a different number.
- Prompt-injection awareness: the hint is raw user text interpolated into an LLM prompt whose output MUST stay valid JSON matching the existing schema. When augmenting _IDENTIFICATION_PROMPT (app/identification.py), the hint must be clearly delimited (e.g. quoted, on its own labeled line such as 'User-provided hint: "..."') and placed BEFORE the final response-format instructions, so the format instructions remain the model's last/most salient instruction. This is a defense-in-depth measure appropriate for this app's stakes, not a hardened security boundary -- do not over-engineer beyond clear delimiting + ordering.
- Frontend rendering of the hint back to the user (result page) must use normal JSX text interpolation ({item.hint}), never dangerouslySetInnerHTML or any raw-HTML injection -- React's default escaping is sufficient and required.

Known limitation, flagged explicitly (not addressed by any bead in this epic -- out of scope): this project has no migration tool (Base.metadata.create_all() only creates missing tables, it does not alter existing ones). Adding the user_hint column means any PRE-EXISTING SQLite DB file (local dev DB, or the already-deployed Railway volume at DATA_DIR) will NOT pick up the new column automatically and the app will error on first read/write touching it. Whoever deploys this change needs to either delete/recreate the DB file or manually ALTER TABLE -- call this out in the PR description when this epic ships; no bead should attempt to build a migration system as part of this work.

title: Restyle frontend with Tailwind CSS for a nice, fresh, modern look
description:
WHY: The app works end-to-end (photo upload, identification, Kleinanzeigen
search, pricing decision, results view, inventory) but its styling is
plain hand-written CSS (frontend/src/App.css, ~200 lines) built
incrementally across several beads with no shared design system --
functional, not "nice, fresh, modern" as requested.

HIGH-LEVEL DESIGN: adopt Tailwind CSS as the styling framework and
restyle the existing pages/components in place, without changing their
behavior, data flow, or test coverage. Sequence: install & wire up
Tailwind -> define a small shared design system (colors incl. the
existing sell/give-away/throw-away semantic colors, type scale,
spacing) as reusable Tailwind theme config -> restyle each page against
that shared system -> restyle shared chrome (nav/layout/PWA theme
color) -> remove the now-dead legacy CSS -> a final visual QA pass
(screenshots + console-error check across all pages).

EXISTING PAGES TO RESTYLE (frontend/src/):
- UploadPage.jsx -- photo capture/upload flow
- ItemResultPage.jsx -- per-item results (photo, decision badge,
  suggested price, comparable listings)
- InventoryPage.jsx -- item list with status/decision filters and
  status-transition action buttons
- App.jsx -- router root / shared nav

EXISTING SEMANTIC COLORS TO PRESERVE (from App.css, currently ad hoc --
this epic's design-tokens task should carry these into Tailwind theme
config deliberately, not invent new ones): sell = green, give_away =
blue, throw_away = red (see the decision badges visible in the
screenshots already shared with the user this session).

FLAGGED ASSUMPTIONS / OPEN QUESTIONS (not silently resolved):
1. Tailwind CSS version/setup approach (v4's CSS-first @theme config +
   Vite plugin vs. v3's tailwind.config.js) is left to the install task
   to research and pick the current recommended approach for a Vite +
   React project, documenting the choice -- don't assume a specific
   version without checking what's current.
2. Dark mode is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for this epic -- "nice, fresh,
   modern" does not imply dark mode support unless the user asks
   separately. Don't add it speculatively.
3. No new npm packages beyond Tailwind and its direct build-tooling
   dependencies (e.g. the Vite plugin) -- no component libraries
   (shadcn/ui, daisyUI, etc.) unless a later task explicitly decides
   one is needed and documents why; default to plain Tailwind utility
   classes.
4. Responsive design: the app is phone-camera-first (see root README's
   "the whole point of this app is taking photos with a phone camera"),
   so mobile-width layouts are the PRIMARY target, not an afterthought
   -- each restyle task's done-criteria requires checking a mobile
   viewport (~375-420px wide), not just desktop.

DONE WHEN: all four pages/components above are restyled with Tailwind
utility classes following the shared design tokens, the legacy
App.css is removed (or reduced to only what Tailwind itself needs),
all existing frontend tests still pass unmodified in behavior, and a
final visual QA pass confirms no console errors and consistent styling
across pages via screenshots.

title: Basement Declutter App: photo -> Kleinanzeigen search -> sell/give-away/throw-away decision
description:
WHY: Personal tool to clear out a basement. User photographs an item; the
app identifies it, checks what comparable items go for on Kleinanzeigen
(German classifieds; no official public API), and recommends one of three
actions with a suggested price where relevant: (a) sell for <price>,
(b) give away, (c) throw away.

RECOMMENDED STACK (for review, not final until T1 spike resolves the
Kleinanzeigen access question):
- Backend: Python + FastAPI. Chosen over Node because the scraping
  ecosystem (httpx, BeautifulSoup, Playwright) and typical vision-API
  client libraries are strongest in Python, and it keeps one language
  across identification, scraping, and pricing logic.
- Frontend: Mobile-first PWA (React + Vite or plain HTML/JS), camera
  capture via <input capture> / getUserMedia, installable on a phone
  home screen. No native app / app-store distribution for an MVP used
  by one person.
- Vision/item identification: a vision-capable LLM (e.g. Claude with
  image input) given the photo, returning structured JSON: name,
  category, brand guess, condition guess, search keywords.
- Kleinanzeigen data access: NO official public API exists (Kleinanzeigen
  shut down third-party API access years ago). Some access method
  (scraping via Playwright, or an existing unofficial wrapper) will be
  required. This carries real ToS / bot-protection / legal-gray-area
  risk that is NOT resolved here -- see T1.
- Pricing/decision engine: simple rule-based logic over scraped
  comparable listings (e.g. median of active comparable prices), with
  configurable thresholds separating sell / give-away / throw-away.

title: Fix ~6% flaky failure in test_session_token_tampered_returns_none
description: backend/tests/test_auth.py's test_session_token_tampered_returns_none 'tampers' a valid session token by replacing its LAST character with 'x', then asserts verify_session_token() returns None. This fails intermittently (~1/16, ~6.25%, reproduced 2/30 and 1/8 in stress runs) -- NOT an auth bypass. Root cause (confirmed empirically by the reviewer, 129/2000 token last-chars all 'w'): the token's final base64url segment encodes a 20-byte HMAC-SHA1 signature; its last character carries only 4 significant bits plus 2 non-canonical padding bits that Python's base64 decoder does not reject. Mutating that specific character from 'w' to 'x' sometimes decodes to IDENTICAL signature bytes (since the two differ only in the ignored padding bits), so the 'tampered' token is byte-identical after decoding and legitimately re-verifies. Issued tokens' last char is one of 16 possible values (all differing in ignorable padding bits), so this specific mutation has a structural 1/16 chance of producing a no-op 'tamper'. Security impact: none -- payload tampering (any character earlier in the token) is caught reliably; this only affects the specific choice of which character this one test happens to flip.
acceptance_criteria: test_session_token_tampered_returns_none mutates a character elsewhere in the token (e.g. a character in the payload segment, or any position other than the last base64 group's padding-bit-only tail) so the mutation is guaranteed to change the decoded bytes. Stress-test the fix: run the test 100+ times in a loop (or seed multiple distinct tampered variants within the test) and confirm zero failures. No production code changes needed -- this is purely a test-construction bug.

title: Wire listing-text generation into the pipeline before the DECIDED commit
description:
Depends on sandbox-dwl.1 (columns) and sandbox-dwl.2 (`ListingTextService.generate_listing_text(item) -> bool` must already exist and work). File: backend/app/pipeline.py.

Read backend/app/pipeline.py's `run_pipeline` function in full first, specifically stage 3 ("pricing/decision"). Confirmed by prior investigation: `PricingDecisionService.decide_item(item)` already sets `item.status = ItemStatus.DECIDED` itself, in memory, as part of computing the decision -- BEFORE `run_pipeline`'s own `session.commit()` call that follows it. This means the ordering invariant (suggested_title/description must be in their final state by the time a client observes status=decided) is achievable with a small, precisely-placed insertion -- no restructuring of pricing.py needed.

1. In `run_pipeline`, stage 3, insert a call to the new listing-text service AFTER `pricing_service.decide_item(item)` returns and BEFORE the `session.commit()` that currently follows it directly. Add a `listing_text_service: ListingTextService | None = None` parameter to `run_pipeline` (and thread it through `run_pipeline_with_new_session` too), matching the existing pattern for `identification_service`/`search_service`/`pricing_service` (default to `ListingTextService()` when not provided, exactly like the others).
2. Call `listing_text_service.generate_listing_text(item)` unconditionally at that point -- the service itself already handles the decision-gating (no-op for throw_away/pending) and never raises, so `pipeline.py` doesn't need its own conditional or try/except around this call; just call it and let it do its job.
3. Do NOT change what happens on the return value -- unlike the identification/search stages, a `False` return from `generate_listing_text` must NOT halt the pipeline or change any status (this is a best-effort enhancement layered on an already-complete decision, not a gate). The existing `session.commit()` and the "Pipeline completed" log line that follow should run exactly as they do today, regardless of whether listing-text generation succeeded.
4. Update `run_pipeline`'s docstring (the "Stage-by-stage behavior" section) to document this new sub-step within stage 3 -- brief, matching the existing docstring's level of detail for the other stages.
5. Tests in backend/tests/test_pipeline.py (extend the existing file, follow its conventions -- it already injects fake identification/search/pricing services per test):
   - A full pipeline run ending in decision=SELL: pass a fake `listing_text_service` (or a real `ListingTextService` with an injected fake provider, whichever matches this test file's existing style for the other stages) that returns `True` and sets fields -- assert the final committed `Item` has `suggested_title`/`suggested_description` populated AND `status == ItemStatus.DECIDED`, confirming both land in the SAME commit (i.e., don't just check the fields are eventually set -- confirm they're present in the item as read back from a fresh query immediately after the pipeline call returns, proving no extra commit/round-trip was needed).
   - Same for decision=GIVE_AWAY.
   - decision=THROW_AWAY: assert `suggested_title`/`suggested_description` remain `None` and the pipeline still completes normally (status reaches DECIDED, no error).
   - The listing-text stage failing (fake service call raises, or returns `False`): assert the pipeline still completes normally -- item still reaches `status=DECIDED` with its decision/price intact, `suggested_title`/`suggested_description` are `None`, and (critically) NO EXCEPTION propagates out of `run_pipeline` -- this is the single most important regression to guard against, since a bug here would take down the entire pipeline over what should be a non-critical enhancement.
6. Run the full backend pytest suite (`cd backend && source .venv/bin/activate && python -m pytest -q`) and confirm all pass -- report the exact count.

Done-criteria: listing-text generation runs after decide_item() and before the stage-3 commit (verified by a test proving both land in the same committed snapshot), a failure/false-return in this stage never halts the pipeline or raises, throw_away items are correctly skipped, full pytest suite green (report count).

Reviewer verified the exact call ordering by line number, confirmed POST /items needs zero changes, and mutation-tested the try/except by removing it -- the raising-fake test failed as expected (assert pending_decision == decided), proving the guard is load-bearing. 238/238 passing. title: Build the listing-text generation service
description:
Depends on sandbox-dwl.1 (Item.suggested_title/suggested_description columns must already exist). New file: backend/app/listing_text.py. New test file: backend/tests/test_listing_text.py.

Read backend/app/identification.py in full first -- this bead mirrors its exact architecture (Provider Protocol + injectable-fake pattern, lazy Anthropic client construction, Service class that never raises). Match that file's structure and conventions closely rather than inventing a different shape.

1. Define a `ListingTextProvider` Protocol (mirroring `IdentificationProvider`) with a method that takes the structured item info and returns a dict with `title`/`description` keys (or whatever shape reads cleanest -- your call, but keep it a plain dict like `IdentificationProvider.identify()` does, not a Pydantic model, for consistency with the existing pattern).
2. Implement `ClaudeListingTextProvider` (mirroring `ClaudeVisionProvider`): lazily constructs an `anthropic.Anthropic` client (so importing this module never requires `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` to be set, exactly like `ClaudeVisionProvider._get_client()`), reuses the SAME model config as identification (read `ANTHROPIC_VISION_MODEL` env var / the same default model constant -- do not introduce a new env var for model selection). This is a TEXT-ONLY call (no image content block) -- send only text: the item's `identified_name`, `category`, `brand`, `condition`, `search_keywords`, `decision`, `suggested_price`. Prompt requirements (write this prompt carefully, it's the core of the feature):
   - Output must be German.
   - Output must be a single JSON object (no prose, no markdown fences) with exactly `"title"` and `"description"` string keys -- match `_IDENTIFICATION_PROMPT`'s existing "respond with ONLY a single JSON object" instruction style in identification.py.
   - Title should target <=65 characters (Kleinanzeigen's real title UI limit) -- instruct the model explicitly, but see point 4 for the code-level enforcement (do not rely on the prompt alone).
   - Description should be a few sentences: what the item is, its condition, and (for decision=sell) a price framing appropriate for a German classifieds ad (e.g. mentioning the price and, if it reads naturally, "VB" -- Verhandlungsbasis/negotiable, a standard German classifieds convention) or (for decision=give_away) that it's free / "zu verschenken".
   - If comparable listings are available and would help ground the tone/style, you may optionally include 1-2 of their titles as style reference in the prompt -- this is optional, not required; skip it if it complicates the prompt more than it helps.
3. Implement `ListingTextService` (mirroring `ItemIdentificationService`): a `generate_listing_text(item) -> bool` method (matching `identify_item`'s exact return-bool-never-raise contract) that:
   - Returns `False` immediately (no LLM call) if `item.decision` is not SELL or GIVE_AWAY -- this stage is a no-op for throw_away/pending items. Do NOT touch `suggested_title`/`suggested_description` in this case (leave them as whatever they already were, which should be `None`).
   - Otherwise calls the provider. On ANY exception from the provider (network error, parse error, malformed response, missing API key -- catch broadly, matching `identify_item`'s `except Exception` pattern), log it (matching the existing `logger.exception(...)` style) and return `False` WITHOUT raising -- `suggested_title`/`suggested_description` stay `None`.
   - On success, extract `title`/`description` from the returned dict. If either is missing/empty/not a string, treat this as a failure (return `False`, leave both fields `None`) -- do not partially populate one field without the other.
   - Apply the code-level title-length safety clamp here (not relying on the prompt alone): if the returned title exceeds 65 characters, truncate it sensibly (e.g. at a word boundary if reasonably close to the limit, otherwise a hard truncation) -- write a small helper function for this and unit-test it directly with a few length cases (well under limit, exactly at limit, well over limit, over limit with a convenient word boundary nearby).
   - On success, sets `item.suggested_title`/`item.suggested_description` and returns `True`. Does NOT commit (matches the existing convention -- the caller, pipeline.py, owns the session lifecycle, per identification.py's own module docstring pattern).
4. Tests in backend/tests/test_listing_text.py, following test_identification.py's existing conventions closely (a `_StubProvider`/fake pattern, no real network calls):
   - `decision=THROW_AWAY` -> `generate_listing_text` returns `False`, no provider call made at all, fields untouched.
   - `decision=PENDING` -> same (no-op).
   - `decision=SELL` with a fake provider returning a valid `{"title": ..., "description": ...}` -> returns `True`, both fields set correctly.
   - `decision=GIVE_AWAY` with a fake provider -> same, returns `True`, fields set.
   - Fake provider raising an exception -> returns `False`, both fields remain `None`, no exception propagates out of `generate_listing_text`.
   - Fake provider returning a malformed dict (missing `title` key, or `description` is not a string, or empty title) -> returns `False`, fields remain `None`.
   - Title-clamping helper: direct unit tests for the length cases described in point 3.
   - Confirm the real `ClaudeListingTextProvider` can be constructed/imported with no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set (matching `ClaudeVisionProvider`'s existing test coverage for this same property -- find and mirror that test).
5. Run the full backend pytest suite (`cd backend && source .venv/bin/activate && python -m pytest -q`) and confirm all pass -- report the exact count.

Done-criteria: `app/listing_text.py` exists following identification.py's architecture, the German/JSON/title-length prompt requirements are all present, the never-raises/decision-gated/malformed-response-handling contract is fully tested with an injectable fake (no real network calls), the title-clamping safety net is unit-tested directly, full pytest suite green (report count).
close_reason: Added backend/app/listing_text.py mirroring identification.py's exact architecture: ClaudeListingTextProvider (text-only, lazy client, reuses ANTHROPIC_VISION_MODEL, German/JSON-only prompt with a 65-char title target) and ListingTextService.generate_listing_text() (decision-gated to SELL/GIVE_AWAY, never raises, rejects malformed responses without partial writes, code-level title clamp). Reviewer intercepted the real Claude API call to confirm text-only content, quoted the exact rendered prompt for both decisions, ran a dozen independent clamp-boundary tests (including a 200-char single word with no spaces, always <=65), mutation-tested the never-raises contract with adversarial exception types, and confirmed the malformed-response tests are 5 genuinely distinct, non-duplicated cases. 233/233 passing. Filed sandbox-44h for a shared, pre-existing, non-blocking hardening gap (non-dict provider response) affecting both this file and identification.py.

title: Migrate UploadPage/ItemResultPage/InventoryPage to apiFetch; add sign-out control
description: Depends on sandbox-dfr.3 (backend routes are actually gated -- otherwise there's nothing to verify end-to-end) and sandbox-dfr.4 (the apiFetch helper and AuthContext must already exist). Files: frontend/src/UploadPage.jsx, frontend/src/ItemResultPage.jsx, frontend/src/InventoryPage.jsx. Goal: every existing API call in these three pages goes through apiFetch (from sandbox-dfr.4) instead of a raw fetch, so the Authorization header is actually attached -- without this bead, sandbox-dfr.3's newly-gated backend routes would make the whole app appear broken (every request would 401) even though sandbox-dfr.4's sign-in flow works. 1. Grep each of the three files for their existing fetch( calls (there are four total across these three files, per this app's current structure -- confirm the exact count yourself, don't assume): replace each with apiFetch(...), preserving each call's existing options (method, headers, body) exactly, just swapping the function and adjusting the path argument to match apiFetch's signature (check exactly what apiFetch expects for its first argument -- a path relative to API_BASE_URL, or a full URL -- from sandbox-dfr.4's implementation, and adjust each call site's URL construction accordingly, e.g. dropping the now-redundant ${API_BASE_URL} prefix if apiFetch already adds it internally). 2. For each call site, confirm the existing error-handling logic (e.g. extractErrorMessage, status-code checks) still works correctly given apiFetch's return value is a normal Response object (per sandbox-dfr.4's contract) -- it should need no changes if apiFetch is a thin wrapper, but verify this by actually reading the surrounding code, not just assuming. 3. Add explicit handling for the "session expired mid-use" case: if apiFetch returns a 401 for one of these page-level requests (e.g. the user's session expired while they had the app open in a background tab), the page should surface a sensible message rather than treating it like an unrelated fetch failure. Since apiFetch already clears the stale token from localStorage on a 401 (per sandbox-dfr.4), and the AuthContext is the source of truth for isAuthenticated... check whether the AuthContext needs a way to be notified/re-checked from these pages (e.g. an exported "trigger a re-check" function) so the app-level gate in App.jsx correctly reverts to the sign-in page on the NEXT render after a 401 happens deep inside one of these pages, rather than requiring a manual refresh. If sandbox-dfr.4's AuthContext already handles this reactively (e.g. it re-checks /auth/me periodically, or listens for a custom event, or apiFetch itself could dispatch something the AuthContext listens for), use that; if not, this bead should add the minimal glue needed (e.g. apiFetch dispatching a window CustomEvent on 401 that AuthContext listens for) -- read sandbox-dfr.4's actual implementation first before deciding what, if anything, is missing. 4. Add a "Sign out" control somewhere reachable from every page (e.g. a small header/nav element showing the signed-in email + a sign-out button/link, added once and shared, or added independently to each of the three pages if this codebase has no shared layout wrapper to hook into -- check App.jsx/index.css for the "Shared layout wrapper: deliberately NOT introduced here" comment already in App.jsx before deciding whether to introduce one now or keep it simple and per-page; prefer the smallest change that gets a working sign-out affordance onto every page without fighting existing per-page layout decisions). 5. **CRITICAL, added after sandbox-dfr.3's review: photo `` tags need an authenticated-fetch fix, or every photo will silently fail to render.** GET /uploads/{filename} (sandbox-dfr.3) now requires an `Authorization: Bearer ` header. `InventoryPage.jsx` and `ItemResultPage.jsx` currently render photos as plain `` (grep both files for the exact current lines) -- a browser's `` tag has NO way to attach a custom header to the request it makes for `src`, so once this ships, every photo request would get a 401 and show a broken-image icon. Do NOT solve this by adding a `?token=` query-parameter fallback on the backend -- that would add a second, weaker auth pathway (tokens leaking into browser history and server access logs) and was deliberately rejected in favor of this approach: keep `Authorization` header as the ONLY auth mechanism, and have the FRONTEND fetch photo bytes authenticated, then render them as a blob URL. - Add a small reusable hook, e.g. `useAuthedImageUrl(photoUrl)` in a new file (e.g. `frontend/src/useAuthedImageUrl.js`) or colocated wherever fits this codebase's existing conventions: given a `photo_url` (relative path from the API), it calls `apiFetch(photoUrl)`, reads the response as a `Blob` (`await response.blob()`), creates an object URL via `URL.createObjectURL(blob)`, and returns that object URL once ready (start in a "loading"/null state, update via `useState`/`useEffect`). On unmount OR when the underlying `photoUrl` changes, call `URL.revokeObjectURL(...)` on the previous object URL to avoid leaking memory -- this matters especially for `InventoryPage.jsx`, which can render many photo thumbnails in a list. - Handle the "photo not ready yet" state sensibly (e.g. `photo_url` may be null/absent for a still-processing item, same as today -- don't fetch in that case) and the "fetch failed" state (e.g. a 401 here should feed into the SAME session-expired handling from point 3, since it's exactly that same failure mode -- reuse whatever mechanism point 3 established, don't build a second one). - Update both `InventoryPage.jsx` and `ItemResultPage.jsx` to use this hook instead of the raw `src={...}` string, rendering nothing/a placeholder while the blob URL is loading (avoid a flash of a broken-image icon during the brief authenticated-fetch round-trip). - Tests: cover the hook directly (mock apiFetch to return a fake Blob response, assert the hook eventually returns an object-URL-shaped string; assert `URL.revokeObjectURL` gets called on unmount/URL change -- you'll need to mock `URL.createObjectURL`/`revokeObjectURL` in the test environment if jsdom doesn't provide them, check first) and update each page's existing photo-rendering tests to account for the new async blob-fetch step (e.g. `waitFor` the img's `src` to become a blob: URL rather than asserting on the raw `photo_url` string like before). 6. Update/extend each page's existing tests (UploadPage.test.jsx, ItemResultPage.test.jsx, InventoryPage.test.jsx) to mock apiFetch instead of/in addition to raw fetch wherever the page under test now calls it -- confirm every existing test still passes with this swap (some may need their mocking approach adjusted, e.g. mocking the api.js module's export instead of global fetch). 7. Add at least one test per page proving a 401 response is handled sensibly (not crashing, not showing a confusing raw error) -- exact expected behavior depends on what point 3 concludes; make the test assert whatever that resolved behavior actually is. 8. title: Add /auth/google, /auth/me, /auth/logout endpoints and the require_user dependency

2. New endpoint `GET /auth/me`:
   - Reads the `Authorization` header, expects `Bearer <token>` format (return 401 if the header is missing or malformed -- not `Bearer <something>`).

Add a reusable FastAPI dependency, e.g. `def require_user(authorization: str | None = Header(None)) -> str` (or via `Depends` with the `Authorization` header, matching FastAPI's standard header-dependency pattern) that: parses the `Bearer <token>` header, calls `verify_session_token`, raises `HTTPException(401, detail=...)` if missing/malformed header or invalid/expired token, and returns the verified email string on success. Factor `GET /auth/me`'s logic to use this SAME dependency (don't duplicate the parsing/verification logic between the two) -- `GET /auth/me` becomes essentially `def get_me(email: str = Depends(require_user)): return {"email": email}`.

Return 200 with an empty/simple body (e.g. `{"ok": true}`). Gate it behind `require_user` too (so calling logout without a valid session is a 401, consistent with everything else) -- document in a one-line comment that this is intentionally a no-op beyond auth-checking, since the frontend is responsible for discarding its own locally-stored token (a later bead's job).

title: Build the auth core: Google ID token verification, whitelist check, session tokens
description:
New file: backend/app/auth.py. New env vars parsed here: GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, ALLOWED_EMAILS, SESSION_SECRET.

1. Add dependencies to backend/requirements.txt: `google-auth` (for verifying Google ID tokens against Google's public keys) and `itsdangerous` (for signing our own session tokens). Match this repo's existing pinning style (check requirements.txt for the range-pin convention already used for alembic).

2. Parse ALLOWED_EMAILS the same way ALLOWED_ORIGINS is already parsed in app/main.py (grep `_parse_allowed_origins` for the exact convention to mirror: comma-separated, strips whitespace around each entry, case handling). Write `_parse_allowed_emails(raw: str | None) -> list[str]` in app/auth.py: splits on commas, strips whitespace, lowercases every entry (email whitelist matching must be case-insensitive), drops empty entries. Unlike ALLOWED_ORIGINS (which has a non-empty default), ALLOWED_EMAILS must default to an EMPTY list when unset -- there is no sensible non-empty default for a security whitelist (fail-closed).

3. Write `verify_google_id_token(id_token_str: str) -> str`:
   - Verifies the token via `google.oauth2.id_token.verify_oauth2_token(id_token_str, google.auth.transport.requests.Request(), audience=GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID)` (or equivalent) -- this checks the signature against Google's public keys and the `aud` claim matches our GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID.
   - Raises a custom `AuthError` (define this exception class in this module) if: the token is malformed/invalid/expired/signature fails (whatever the verify call raises -- catch broadly and re-raise as AuthError with a clear message, matching this codebase's pattern in app/identification.py's IdentificationError), OR the verified payload's `email_verified` claim is not True, OR the verified email (case-insensitively) is not in the current ALLOWED_EMAILS list (re-read the env var at call time via a small `_allowed_emails()` helper, not a module-level constant computed once at import -- so a redeployed env var change takes effect without needing anything besides a normal restart, matching this codebase's `os.environ.get(...)` read-at-call-time convention used elsewhere, e.g. `_default_db_path()`).
   - On success, returns the verified email string (lowercased).
   - GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID itself: if unset/empty, `verify_google_id_token` must always raise AuthError (fail closed -- can't verify an audience against nothing).

4. Write `issue_session_token(email: str) -> str` and `verify_session_token(token: str) -> str | None`:
   - `issue_session_token`: signs a payload containing the email and issued-at info using `itsdangerous.URLSafeTimedSerializer(SESSION_SECRET)` (read SESSION_SECRET from the environment at call time, same lazy-read convention as above). If SESSION_SECRET is unset/empty, raise a clear `RuntimeError` at call time (this is a hard misconfiguration, not a soft-fail case -- signing tokens with no secret would be insecure).
   - `verify_session_token`: deserializes with a max_age matching a SESSION_MAX_AGE_SECONDS constant (7 days in seconds, defined once at module level with a comment). Returns the email string on success, or `None` on ANY failure (expired, tampered, malformed, wrong secret) -- callers treat `None` as "not authenticated", never raise out of this function (matching the "predictable None vs exception" pattern used elsewhere in this codebase, e.g. `_is_low_confidence` returning a plain bool rather than raising).

5. Tests in backend/tests/test_auth.py (new file):
   - `_parse_allowed_emails`: empty/None input -> `[]`; whitespace/casing normalization; comma-separated parsing.
   - `verify_google_id_token`: since we can't call the real Google network from tests, inject a fake verifier the same way `ClaudeVisionProvider` accepts an injectable `client` -- refactor `verify_google_id_token` to accept an optional `verify_fn` parameter (defaulting to the real `google.oauth2.id_token.verify_oauth2_token`) so tests can pass a fake that returns a canned payload dict without hitting the network. Cover: valid token + whitelisted + verified email -> returns email; valid token + email NOT in whitelist -> AuthError; valid token + `email_verified: False` -> AuthError; ALLOWED_EMAILS unset/empty -> AuthError even for an otherwise-valid token; GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID unset -> AuthError; the fake verify_fn raising an exception (simulating a real verification failure, e.g. bad signature) -> AuthError.
   - `issue_session_token`/`verify_session_token`: round-trip (issue then verify returns the same email); tampered token (flip a character) -> `verify_session_token` returns None; expired token (use itsdangerous's ability to specify a fake "issued at" or monkeypatch time, or construct with a very small max_age and sleep past it, or directly test via a manually-crafted expired signed value) -> returns None; SESSION_SECRET unset -> `issue_session_token` raises RuntimeError.

6. Run the full backend pytest suite (`cd backend && source .venv/bin/activate && python -m pytest -q`) and confirm all pass (should be 177 + your new tests, e.g. ~187-190 depending on how many you write -- report the exact final count).

Done-criteria: backend/app/auth.py exists with the four functions/behaviors above, all fail-closed defaults verified (ALLOWED_EMAILS unset -> deny, GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID unset -> deny, SESSION_SECRET unset -> hard error not silent insecurity), comprehensive tests using an injectable fake verifier (no real network calls to Google in tests), full pytest suite green (report exact count).

Reviewer reproduced all fail-closed paths adversarially, confirmed lazy env-var reads at every call site, mutation-tested the expiry check (removing max_age broke the test), corrected the implementer's 'no linter' claim (ruff is available and clean). 197/197 passing.

title: Enable Alembic batch mode for SQLite so future migrations can alter/drop columns
description: backend/alembic/env.py does not set render_as_batch=True on its context.configure() calls. SQLite doesn't support most ALTER TABLE operations natively (dropping/renaming/retyping a column) -- Alembic's 'batch' mode works around this by creating a new table, copying data, and swapping it in, but only when render_as_batch=True is set. Right now the only migration in the chain is an ADD COLUMN (which SQLite does support directly), so this hasn't bitten us yet -- but any future migration doing more than a plain add-column (e.g. dropping the old suggested_price Float column and replacing it with a Numeric, or renaming a column) will fail outright without batch mode. Flagged by the reviewer during sandbox-64f.2's review as a real, not hypothetical, risk given this epic's stated purpose (future schema evolution).
acceptance_criteria: backend/alembic/env.py's context.configure() calls (both run_migrations_offline and run_migrations_online) pass render_as_batch=True. A test or manual verification demonstrates a migration that drops/alters a column succeeds against a SQLite DB after this change (e.g. a throwaway migration exercised in a test, then removed, or a documented manual repro) -- prove it actually works, don't just add the flag on faith. No change to the existing migration chain's behavior/output for the current ADD COLUMN migration (batch mode is a superset capability, should be a no-op for operations SQLite already supports directly).

title: Add a tested, idempotent 'upgrade to head' entrypoint that reconciles pre-Alembic DBs
description:
Depends on sandbox-64f.2 (both migration revisions must already exist to test against). New file: backend/app/db_migrate.py. New test file: backend/tests/test_db_migrate.py.

Goal: one function that, given a DB URL, brings that DB to Alembic 'head' correctly regardless of which of three states it's currently in, and is safe to call repeatedly (idempotent). This is the function that will later run as a pre-start deploy step (task 4) and is what will eventually reconcile the live Railway DB (not this bead's job to run against Railway itself -- Railway access is unavailable this session, see the epic description).

1. Create backend/app/db_migrate.py with:
   - A function 'upgrade_to_head(database_url: str) -> None' (or 'db_url' -- match this codebase's existing naming, e.g. app/db.py's make_engine(db_url=...) param name) that:
     a. Builds an Alembic Config pointing at backend/alembic.ini, with 'sqlalchemy.url' set to the given 'database_url' (via 'config.set_main_option("sqlalchemy.url", database_url)') -- this must work regardless of current working directory (resolve alembic.ini's path relative to this file's location, e.g. 'Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "alembic.ini"', not a relative string that breaks if invoked from a different cwd).
     b. Opens a connection to that URL (e.g. via 'sqlalchemy.create_engine(database_url).connect()') and uses Alembic's 'MigrationContext.configure(connection)' to read 'get_current_revision()'.
     c. If 'get_current_revision()' is None (no alembic_version table / never tracked):
        - Inspect the DB (e.g. 'sqlalchemy.inspect(engine).has_table("items")') to distinguish a genuinely fresh/empty DB from a legacy pre-Alembic DB that already has tables.
        - If 'items' table already exists: this is a legacy DB -- stamp it at the baseline revision (the actual revision id of the '0001'-equivalent migration from sandbox-64f.2 -- do not hardcode a guessed id string, read it from Alembic's script directory, e.g. via 'alembic.script.ScriptDirectory.from_config(cfg).get_revisions("base")' or by walking down_revision==None) via 'alembic.command.stamp(cfg, <that revision id>)'. This must be a true no-op against that exact schema (relies on sandbox-64f.2 being correct) -- do NOT execute revision 0001's actual DDL against a DB that already has those tables (that would error, tables already exist).
        - If 'items' table does NOT exist: genuinely fresh DB, do nothing extra here -- 'upgrade head' below will run every revision from scratch.
     d. Always finish with 'alembic.command.upgrade(cfg, "head")' -- this is the actual work: for a freshly-stamped legacy DB, this applies only 0002+ (since 0001 was stamped, not executed); for a fresh DB, this applies 0001 then 0002; for a DB already at head, this is a no-op.
   - Also add a small CLI entrypoint so this can be invoked as 'python -m app.db_migrate' (used by task 4's Docker CMD): 'if __name__ == "__main__": upgrade_to_head(get_database_url())' (import get_database_url from app.db, sandbox-64f.1).

title: Generate the baseline + add-user_hint migration chain via autogenerate
description:
Depends on sandbox-64f.1 (Alembic scaffolding + get_database_url() must already exist). Files: backend/alembic/versions/ (two new migration files created here), git history (read-only, for reference).

Goal: produce exactly two migration files that, applied in order to an empty DB, reconstruct today's full schema (including user_hint) -- generated via autogenerate, never hand-typed, so they can't drift from the real model definitions.

Exact recipe:
1. Note the git commit 'ad8bd91' -- this is the last commit BEFORE sandbox-iec.1 added the user_hint column (i.e. backend/app/models.py at that commit has every current table/column EXCEPT Item.user_hint). Confirm this yourself: 'git show ad8bd91:backend/app/models.py | grep -n user_hint' should print nothing; 'git show ad8bd91:backend/app/models.py | grep -n "class Item"' should show the Item class without a user_hint column.
2. Generate revision 0001 (the pre-hint baseline) against that OLD schema:
   a. Save a copy of the CURRENT backend/app/models.py (e.g. 'cp backend/app/models.py /tmp/current_models.py.bak').
   b. Temporarily overwrite backend/app/models.py with the pre-hint version: 'git show ad8bd91:backend/app/models.py > backend/app/models.py'.
   c. Point Alembic at a throwaway empty DB (e.g. via 'DATA_DIR=/tmp/alembic-gen-1 alembic revision --autogenerate -m "baseline schema"' -- pick any throwaway DATA_DIR that doesn't already have a declutter.db file, so autogenerate diffs against a genuinely empty DB).
   d. This produces a new file in backend/alembic/versions/ with 'down_revision = None' -- this is revision 0001. Open it and sanity-check it contains 'op.create_table("items", ...)' (and every other table) with NO user_hint column, plus create_table calls for every other model (grep the file for table names and cross-check against backend/app/models.py's OLD version to confirm nothing is missing).
   e. Restore the current models.py: 'cp /tmp/current_models.py.bak backend/app/models.py' (verify with 'git diff backend/app/models.py' showing no changes vs HEAD after this restore).
3. Generate revision 0002 (add user_hint) against the CURRENT (post-hint) schema, diffed against a DB already at 0001:
   a. Point Alembic at a fresh throwaway DB and bring it to 0001: 'DATA_DIR=/tmp/alembic-gen-2 alembic upgrade head' (with current/restored models.py in place and only revision 0001 existing so far, 'head' == 0001 -- this creates every table except user_hint in that throwaway DB).
   b. Now autogenerate against that same DATA_DIR: 'DATA_DIR=/tmp/alembic-gen-2 alembic revision --autogenerate -m "add user_hint column"' -- since the DB at /tmp/alembic-gen-2 is at 0001 (no user_hint) and the current models.py DOES have user_hint, the diff should detect EXACTLY one change.
   c. This produces revision 0002 with 'down_revision' pointing at 0001's revision id. Open it and confirm it contains exactly one op: 'op.add_column("items", sa.Column("user_hint", sa.String(), nullable=True))' (or equivalent) -- and nothing else. If it contains anything else, something in step 2 was wrong (an extra/missing table or column) -- stop and re-derive rather than hand-editing the file to force it to look right.
4. Correctness check -- prove the two-revision chain exactly reconstructs Base.metadata with nothing missing and nothing extra:
   a. Fresh throwaway DB: 'DATA_DIR=/tmp/alembic-gen-3 alembic upgrade head' (applies 0001 then 0002).
   b. 'DATA_DIR=/tmp/alembic-gen-3 alembic revision --autogenerate -m "empty diff check"' -- this MUST produce a migration file containing an empty 'upgrade()'/'downgrade()' body (or a comment saying no changes detected, depending on Alembic's exact autogenerate output for a no-op diff). If it detects ANY difference, the chain is wrong -- go back and fix revisions 0001/0002, do not commit a broken baseline.
   c. Delete this throwaway 'empty diff check' migration file -- it must NOT be committed, it was only a verification step.
5. Clean up: delete the /tmp/alembic-gen-* directories used for generation. Confirm 'git status' shows exactly two new files under backend/alembic/versions/ (plus whatever sandbox-64f.1 already added) and backend/app/models.py shows NO diff from HEAD (fully restored).
6. Run the full backend pytest suite and confirm it is unchanged (these migration files aren't imported/exercised by any test yet -- that's task 3's job) -- this is just confirming nothing was left broken by the temporary models.py swap.

Done-criteria: exactly two new migration files exist (0001 baseline matching the pre-hint schema, 0002 adding user_hint), both generated via autogenerate per the recipe above (not hand-typed), the empty-diff verification in step 4 passed and its throwaway file was deleted, models.py is byte-identical to HEAD afterward, full pytest suite passes unchanged.

Reviewer independently reproduced the empty-diff verification from scratch, plus a belt-and-braces column-level PRAGMA table_info cross-check against a create_all()-built DB confirming exact column match. 172/172 tests unchanged, models.py confirmed byte-identical to HEAD via sha256. title: Add production Dockerfiles for Railway deploy (backend/Dockerfile.railway, frontend/Dockerfile.railway)
description: Railway's build system detects and unconditionally uses backend/Dockerfile and frontend/Dockerfile whenever they exist in a service's root directory -- setting dockerfilePath:null on the Railway service config does NOT suppress this; confirmed live via build logs ('load build definition from backend/Dockerfile' / 'from frontend/Dockerfile') despite Railpack buildCommand/startCommand being configured. This causes two concrete failures: (1) frontend/Dockerfile has no build step at all (just 'npm install' + 'npm run dev'), so no dist/ directory is ever produced, breaking the 'npx serve -s dist' start command; (2) both Dockerfiles use JSON-array ('exec form') CMD, e.g. CMD ["uvicorn", ..., "--port", "8000"] -- Railway's startCommand override replaces this with a literal string that is NOT passed through a shell, so $PORT is never expanded and the app crashes with e.g. "Invalid value for '--port': '$PORT' is not a valid integer". The existing Dockerfiles are correctly dev-oriented (used by docker-compose.yml for local dev) and must NOT be changed. Instead, add separate production-oriented Dockerfiles that Railway will be explicitly pointed at via dockerfilePath.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New file backend/Dockerfile.railway: production image for the FastAPI backend. Installs requirements.txt, copies only app/ (tests/pytest.ini not required for a production image but harmless if included), EXPOSEs a port, and uses a SHELL-FORM CMD (no JSON array) so $PORT expands at container start, e.g. 'CMD uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port ${PORT:-8000}'. Must NOT modify the existing backend/Dockerfile (that stays as the dev/docker-compose image). 2) New file frontend/Dockerfile.railway: MULTI-STAGE build for the Vite/React frontend. Build stage: node image, 'npm ci', copy source, then 'RUN npm run build' to actually produce dist/. Runtime stage: copy only the built dist/ output, install/run 'serve' (e.g. via npx), with a SHELL-FORM CMD so $PORT expands, e.g. 'CMD npx serve -s dist -l ${PORT:-3000}'. CRITICAL: Vite bakes VITE_* env vars into the JS bundle at BUILD time via import.meta.env, and Railway does NOT automatically forward service environment variables into a Dockerfile build unless the Dockerfile explicitly declares them as ARG and promotes them to ENV before the build step runs. The build stage MUST include 'ARG VITE_API_BASE_URL' followed by 'ENV VITE_API_BASE_URL=$VITE_API_BASE_URL' BEFORE the 'RUN npm run build' line, so that when Railway (or any caller) passes --build-arg VITE_API_BASE_URL=<url>, Vite picks it up. Must NOT modify the existing frontend/Dockerfile (that stays as the dev/docker-compose image with no build step). 3) Do not change docker-compose.yml, README.md, or any other file that references the existing (dev) Dockerfiles -- this is purely additive. 4) Since there's no live Docker daemon in this sandbox, you cannot actually run 'docker build' -- instead verify correctness by careful manual review: read the existing Dockerfiles for the base image/dependency list to mirror, and paste/trace through the exact shell-form CMD syntax to confirm $PORT would genuinely expand (shell form CMD without brackets is implicitly wrapped in /bin/sh -c by Docker -- confirm this is what you wrote, not JSON-array form which does NOT get shell-expanded). Note this explicitly in your report since it can't be build-tested here. 5) Add a short note to README.md's deployment-relevant section (or create one if none exists) documenting these two new Dockerfiles exist specifically for platforms like Railway that build from a Dockerfile and require VITE_API_BASE_URL to be passed as a build arg -- keep this addition brief (a few lines), do not rewrite unrelated README content.
close_reason: Implemented and reviewed: added backend/Dockerfile.railway and frontend/Dockerfile.railway with shell-form CMDs (fixes $PORT expansion) and a multi-stage frontend build with ARG/ENV VITE_API_BASE_URL wired before npm run build. title: Kleinanzeigen search: retry with progressively looser query on zero results
description:

backend/app/identification.py (sandbox-yqf.6).

CONTEXT: reviewer of sandbox-yqf.7 found that identification.py's vision

suitable as search terms" -- i.e. ALTERNATIVE candidate queries a human
might try one at a time -- but comparable_search.py's _build_query
(:284-288) ANDs all of them into a single query string via
" ".join(item.search_keywords). Live, a query like "ikea
schreibtischlampe lampe schreibtisch" will very likely return zero real
comparables even when the item is genuinely resellable, which silently
biases the downstream decision engine (sandbox-yqf.8) toward
throw_away/give_away for items that would actually sell fine.

This is a quality/accuracy issue, not a correctness bug -- the current
zero-results path IS correctly implemented and tested (empty list,
status still advances to pending_decision). This bead is about making
zero real results less likely to be a false negative from over-narrow
querying.

retry with a progressively looser query before giving up: e.g. drop the
last keyword and retry, then try only the first keyword alone, up to a
small bounded number of attempts (do not retry unboundedly -- respect
the existing rate-limiting/backoff already in comparable_search.py).
Stop retrying as soon as any attempt returns >=1 result.

DONE-CRITERIA:
- Existing tests continue to pass unmodified in behavior for their
  cases (non-zero results on first try, hard failures, etc).
- New test: a fixture where the fully-joined query returns zero results
  but a looser query (e.g. first keyword alone) returns >=1 result --
  assert the service returns the non-empty result set, not an empty one.
- New test: a fixture where EVERY progressively looser query returns
  zero results -- assert the service still correctly returns an empty
  list (not an error) and Item.status still advances to pending_decision,
  same as today's zero-results behavior.
- The total number of live search calls attempted per item stays
  bounded (assert an exact upper-bound call count in the all-empty test
  case, so this can't silently become an unbounded retry loop).

title: Harden identification.py/listing_text.py against a non-dict provider response

title: Derive stored upload extension from sniffed image format, not client-supplied header/filename
description:
INPUT: backend/app/main.py's upload endpoint (sandbox-yqf.4, hardened in
sandbox-yqf.16) -- specifically _pick_extension.

CONTEXT: reviewer of sandbox-yqf.16 found a narrow, currently
UNEXPLOITABLE edge case while stress-testing the magic-byte sniffing:
_pick_extension prefers mimetypes.guess_extension(content_type) for the
stored filename's extension, falling back to the client-supplied
filename's suffix for unrecognized image/* content-types. A file with
valid JPEG magic bytes at the start but SVG body content, served with
an unusual content-type like "image/x-weird", would pass the sniff
(bytes start with real JPEG magic) but get stored with a ".svg"
extension (from the client filename), which StaticFiles would then
serve with an SVG content-type.

Reviewer confirmed this is NOT currently exploitable: such a file
cannot simultaneously satisfy the JPEG magic-byte check (which only
requires the FIRST few bytes) and be well-formed SVG/XML (parsing fails
at column 0-4 in the tested cases), so browsers abort rendering before
any embedded script could run. This bead is defense-in-depth, not a
live vulnerability fix.

ACTION: derive the stored file's extension from the SNIFFED image
format (the magic-byte check that already ran and passed) rather than
from the client-supplied Content-Type header or filename -- e.g. if the
sniff matched the JPEG signature, always store as .jpg regardless of
what the client claimed. This removes the extension-mismatch class of
issue entirely rather than relying on "well-formed XML" being
coincidentally hard to also start with valid raster magic bytes.

DONE-CRITERIA:
- _pick_extension (or its replacement) uses the sniffed format, not
  Content-Type/filename, to choose the stored extension.
- Existing upload tests continue to pass.
- New test: a file with valid JPEG magic bytes, an unusual/absent
  Content-Type, and a client-supplied filename ending in a different
  extension (e.g. ".svg" or ".txt") is stored with a .jpg extension
  matching its sniffed format, not the claimed one.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS: differential-tested the refactored magic-byte sniffing logic against a reconstruction of the pre-refactor sandbox-yqf.16 function over 568,447 inputs (exhaustive short prefixes + 400k random + adversarial) -- zero mismatches, confirming no behavioral drift on this security-sensitive function.
